turns.question: How are route parameters like :name captured during tree matching?
turns.text:

report.answer: During registration, node.addRoute detects a ':name' segment via findWildcard (tree.go:135, ~line 240) and node.insertChild creates a distinct node with nType=param whose path field stores the literal wildcard string (e.g. ":name", tree.go:288-317). During matching, node.getValue's `case param:` branch (tree.go ~488-540) scans the current path from its start until the next '/' or end-of-string (`end`), takes that substring as the captured value (optionally URL-unescaping it), and appends a Param{Key: n.path[1:], Value: val} into the params slice, then continues matching deeper for any remaining path segments; catch-all ('*name') nodes work the same way but capture the entire remaining path in a `case catchAll:` branch (tree.go ~552+).
